name: Architecture
solves: predict how people move through a layout
estimate how much natural light reaches a room

tools.name: Space syntax
tools.does: relates movement to how spaces connect
hypotheses: the layout can be drawn as a network of spaces
the link to movement is empirical

tools.name: Daylight factor
tools.does: gives indoor light as a share of outdoor light

notes: drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: Building
solves: make a structure safe against the loads it will meet
estimate heat lost through an envelope

tools.name: Limit state design
tools.does: checks strength and serviceability against factored loads
hypotheses: load combinations and material values come from the governing code
the structure is within the code's scope

tools.name: Steady-state heat loss (U-value)
tools.does: estimates heat flow through a wall or roof
hypotheses: heat storage in the fabric is ignored

tools.name: Critical path method
tools.does: finds the longest chain of dependent tasks
hypotheses: task durations and dependencies are known

notes: drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: Design
solves: shape a product around the people who will use it

tools.name: Human-centred iterative design
tools.does: cycles through understanding users, prototyping and testing

tools.name: Heuristic evaluation
tools.does: finds usability problems by expert inspection
hypotheses: it finds problems but not how often they occur

notes: drafted in session by a model from general knowledge; no source checked; needs specialist review

name: Urban and regional planning
solves: find land suited to a use by combining mapped factors

tools.name: Four-step travel demand model
tools.does: forecasts trips, their destinations, modes and routes
hypotheses: the area is divided into zones
the model is calibrated to counts

tools.name: Map overlay suitability analysis
tools.does: combines mapped criteria to rank sites
hypotheses: the criteria can be put on a common scale
